proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an accepted \(\mathfrak u\), a graph \(D\in\mathfrak D\), and an outcome cell \(y\).  Put
\[
 E=\mathcal C_1(\mathcal I)\cup
   \left\{\sum_{z\in\Omega}p_z-1\right\},
 \qquad
 G=\{p_z:z\in\Omega\}\cup
   \{h_c:\mathcal I(c)=0\},
\]
and
\[
 H=\{p_z:z\in\Omega\}\cup
   \{h_c:\mathcal I(c)=0\}\cup\{F_{D,y}\}.
\]
All three sets are finite because \(\Omega\) and the collection of conditional-independence statements on \(V\) are finite.  Their members have rational coefficients: the conditional-independence minors and \(F_{D,y}\) have integer coefficients by \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}signature}\), and normalization has integer coefficients.

Consider \(S(E,G,H)\).  For a real table \(p\), the simultaneous conditions \(p_z\geq0\) and \(p_z\neq0\) are equivalent to \(p_z>0\).  Likewise, \(h_c(p)\geq0\) because \(h_c\) is a sum of squares, and \(h_c(p)\geq0\) together with \(h_c(p)\neq0\) is equivalent to \(h_c(p)>0\).  Consequently \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}oracle\text{-}model}\) gives the exact set identity
\[
 S(E,G,H)
 =\{p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}:F_{D,y}(p)\neq0\}.
\]
Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}semialgebraic\text{-}decision\text{-}with\text{-}certificates}\).  It terminates and chooses exactly one of the nonempty and empty cases.

In the nonempty case it returns an exactly encoded
\[
 p^\dagger\in
 S(E,G,H)\cap\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}^\Omega
 =\{p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}^\Omega:
 F_{D,y}(p)\neq0\}.
\]
Every marginal probability appearing as a recorded denominator factor in \(B_{D,y}\) or \(B_{D_0,y}\) is a nonempty sum of cells of \(p^\dagger\).  Strict positivity therefore implies
\[
 B_{D,y}(p^\dagger)>0,
 \qquad
 B_{D_0,y}(p^\dagger)>0.
\]
Using \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}signature}\),
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^\dagger)-T_{D_0,y}(p^\dagger)
 =\frac{A_{D,y}(p^\dagger)B_{D_0,y}(p^\dagger)
       -A_{D_0,y}(p^\dagger)B_{D,y}(p^\dagger)}
      {B_{D,y}(p^\dagger)B_{D_0,y}(p^\dagger)}
 =\frac{F_{D,y}(p^\dagger)}
       {B_{D,y}(p^\dagger)B_{D_0,y}(p^\dagger)}\neq0.
\]
This proves the separating conclusion, including all support and division conditions.

In the empty case the returned Positivstellensatz identity certifies that no \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) has \(F_{D,y}(p)\neq0\).  Hence
\[
 F_{D,y}(p)=0
 \qquad\text{for every }p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}.
\]
For any such \(p\), the same strict-positivity argument gives \(B_{D,y}(p)B_{D_0,y}(p)>0\), so the preceding difference identity yields
\[
 T_{D,y}(p)-T_{D_0,y}(p)=0.
\]
Conversely, if these two rational functionals differ at an exact-oracle table, their positive denominators force \(F_{D,y}\neq0\), so that table belongs to \(S(E,G,H)\).  Therefore emptiness is equivalent to universal equality on the relevant positive exact-oracle chamber, establishing completeness of the criterion.  No step infers feasibility from \(F_{D,y}\notin K_{\mathcal I}\); saturated-real-radical nonmembership may concern a different real component or sign chamber.

Fix an accepted input \(\mathfrak u\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), the represented family \(\mathfrak D\) is finite and nonempty.  The number of outcome cells is
\[
 n_Y=\left|\prod_{v\in Y}\Omega_v\right|
     =\prod_{v\in Y}|\Omega_v|<\infty.
\]
Thus there are exactly \(|\mathfrak D|n_Y\) reference comparisons \((D,y)\).  The constructions in \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}signature}\) use finite sums, products, marginalizations, and exact polynomial reductions, so they produce a finite rational circuit and an integer polynomial for every comparison.

For each comparison, a zero normal form is equivalent to \(F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}saturated\text{-}real\text{-}radical}\), this is the rational-coefficient first-order assertion that every real table satisfying all generators of \(J_{\mathcal I}\) and \(s(p)\neq0\) also satisfies \(F_{D,y}(p)=0\).  The procedure in \(\mathrm{lem{:}tarski\text{-}effective\text{-}qe}\) decides this assertion.  Since there are finitely many comparisons, all zero or nonzero normal-form statuses are therefore obtained after finite exact preprocessing.

If every fixed-order normal form is zero, \(\mathrm{lem{:}equality\text{-}branch\text{-}soundness}\) gives, for every \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\),
\[
 T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p)
 \qquad(D\in\mathfrak D,\ y),
\]
and \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}size}\) supplies a finite exactly checkable real-Nullstellensatz and saturation identity for every comparison.  Hence the algorithm terminates on its fast equality branch without a semialgebraic feasibility call.

Suppose that at least one normal form is nonzero.  Membership of the supplied \(p^{\circ}\) in \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^\Omega\) is part of the accepted-input certificate.  Exact rational evaluation of the finitely many signatures therefore terminates.  If some \(F_{D,y}(p^{\circ})\neq0\), Theorem 1 and positivity of the recorded denominators give
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^{\circ})\neq T_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ}),
\]
so the returned rational table is, in particular, an exact real-algebraic separator.

If the supplied table does not separate, apply Theorem 1 in canonical order to every pair having nonzero normal form.  There are at most \(|\mathfrak D|n_Y\) such pairs, and each application terminates.  If one formula is feasible, Theorem 1 returns
\[
 p^\dagger\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}^\Omega
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 T_{D,y}(p^\dagger)\neq T_{D_0,y}(p^\dagger)
\]
for its indexed cell \(y\).  Therefore the two vectors \((T_{D,y}(p^\dagger))_y\) and \((T_{D_0,y}(p^\dagger))_y\) differ.  The algebraic-number encoding and exact sign checks in Theorem 1 certify normalization, strict cell positivity, every bit-one equality, every bit-zero nonvanishing block, and the failed signature.

It remains to analyze the case in which every tested nonzero-normal-form pair is infeasible.  Theorem 1 then proves universal equality for each such pair and supplies its finite semialgebraic infeasibility certificate.  For a zero-normal-form pair, \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}size}\) supplies an identity of the form
\[
 s^N\left(F_{D,y}^{2k}+\sum_iq_i^2\right)
 =\sum_j a_jf_j,
 \qquad
 J_{\mathcal I}=\langle f_1,\ldots,f_\ell\rangle.
\]
Let \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\).  Normalization and the oracle-one equalities give \(f_j(p)=0\).  Strict cell positivity makes every observed marginal denominator positive, hence \(s(p)\neq0\).  Evaluating the identity and dividing by \(s(p)^N\) yields
\[
 F_{D,y}(p)^{2k}+\sum_iq_i(p)^2=0.
\]
All terms are nonnegative, so \(F_{D,y}(p)=0\).  Since \(B_{D,y}(p)B_{D_0,y}(p)>0\),
\[
 T_{D,y}(p)-T_{D_0,y}(p)
 =\frac{F_{D,y}(p)}{B_{D,y}(p)B_{D_0,y}(p)}=0.
\]
Thus all pairs, including both zero- and nonzero-normal-form pairs, agree throughout \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), and the algorithm returns the reference circuit with one finite certificate per comparison.

The two output branches are mutually exclusive: a separator supplies a point where universal equality is false, whereas the equality certificates prove equality at every exact-oracle point.  They are exhaustive because each of the finitely many existential formulas is either feasible or infeasible.  If the intervention law is common to every represented DAG, no separator formula can be feasible, so the algorithm returns the equality branch.  Conversely, equality-branch soundness gives commonality.  This proves the asserted if-and-only-if statement and termination bound.

Finally, \(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}law\text{-}redundancy}\) shows that every \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) is Markov to every \(D\in\mathfrak D\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\), \(T_{D,y}(p)\) is the outcome-cell law obtained from the DAG truncated factorization under \(do(X=x)\).  Therefore, on the equality branch, the observed-law circuit
\[
 \tau(p)=(T_{D_0,y}(p))_y
\]
equals \(P_x(Y)\) for every represented-DAG SCM compatible with the common observational table.  On the separator branch, the same observed law is compatible with the represented DAGs but yields unequal graph-indexed intervention laws, which is the advertised causal ambiguity rather than merely an algebraic discrepancy.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(R\) be a real closed field.  There is an effective quantifier-elimination procedure for first-order formulas in the language of ordered rings with rational coefficients.  In particular, the truth of every closed formula obtained from finitely many rational polynomial equalities and strict or weak inequalities is decidable, and the procedure terminates after finitely many exact algebraic operations.

source.locator: Section 2, Decision method for elementary algebra, pages 15--42

attestation.note: The displayed effective quantifier-elimination consequence is the exact decision fact used; the stable publisher page is supplied.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(R\) be a real closed field and let \(E,G,H\) be finite subsets of \(R[t_1,\ldots,t_k]\).  Write \(\langle E\rangle\) for the ideal generated by \(E\), \(\operatorname{PO}(G)\) for the preordering generated by \(G\), and \(\operatorname{Mon}(H)\) for the multiplicative monoid generated by \(H\).  The basic semialgebraic set
\[
 S(E,G,H)=\{a\in R^k:e(a)=0\ (e\in E),\ g(a)\geq0\ (g\in G),\ h(a)\neq0\ (h\in H)\}
\]
is empty if and only if there exist \(a_0\in\langle E\rangle\), \(b_0\in\operatorname{PO}(G)\), and \(c_0\in\operatorname{Mon}(H)\) such that
\[
 a_0+b_0+c_0^2=0.
\]

attestation.note: The displayed ideal--preordering--monoid form is the specialization used here; the stable DOI is supplied because no source transcription is embedded.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(E,G,H\) be finite subsets of \(\mathbb Q[t_1,\ldots,t_k]\).  There is a terminating exact algorithm deciding whether \(S(E,G,H)\) is empty.  If it is nonempty, the algorithm returns a point in \(S(E,G,H)\cap\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}^k\), encoded by a rational univariate representation together with coordinate minimal polynomials and rational isolating or Thom data.  If it is empty, the algorithm returns a finite identity
\[
 a_0+b_0+c_0^2=0,
 \qquad
 a_0\in\langle E\rangle,
 \quad b_0\in\operatorname{PO}(G),
 \quad c_0\in\operatorname{Mon}(H),
\]
over a finite real algebraic extension of \(\mathbb Q\).  In either branch, the returned sample or identity is decidable by finite exact algebraic-number arithmetic.  Here \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) denotes the real algebraic closure of \(\mathbb Q\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}tarski\text{-}effective\text{-}qe}\) to the closed existential sentence
\[
 \exists t\ \left[
   \bigwedge_{e\in E}e(t)=0
   \ \wedge\ 
   \bigwedge_{g\in G}g(t)\geq0
   \ \wedge\ 
   \bigwedge_{h\in H}h(t)\neq0
 \right].
\]
This terminates and decides emptiness.  Suppose first that the sentence is true over \(\mathbb R\).  Its coefficients are rational, so \(\mathrm{lem{:}real\text{-}closed\text{-}field\text{-}transfer}\) implies that it is true over the real algebraic closure \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) of \(\mathbb Q\).  Hence a point \(t^\dagger\in S(E,G,H)\cap\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}^k\) exists.

To make existence effective, enumerate finite rational univariate representations.  Such a representation consists of a square-free polynomial \(\mu\in\mathbb Q[w]\), rational isolating endpoints and Thom signs selecting one real root \(\alpha\) of \(\mu\), and rational polynomials \(q_0,q_1,\ldots,q_k\) with \(q_0(\alpha)\neq0\), representing
\[
 t_j=\frac{q_j(\alpha)}{q_0(\alpha)},
 \qquad 1\leq j\leq k.
\]
Every tuple of real algebraic numbers has such a representation: the finitely generated extension of \(\mathbb Q\) generated by its coordinates is a finite separable extension, hence has a primitive element, and each selected real algebraic root admits rational isolating endpoints.  For each enumerated code, exact reduction modulo \(\mu\) and exact sign determination from the isolating or Thom data decide every equality and sign condition defining \(S(E,G,H)\).  The code of \(t^\dagger\) is eventually enumerated, so the search terminates.  Resultants followed by square-free factorization give a minimal polynomial and isolating data for every coordinate, as claimed.

Suppose instead that the sentence is false.  Then \(S(E,G,H)\) is empty over \(\mathbb R\), and by \(\mathrm{lem{:}real\text{-}closed\text{-}field\text{-}transfer}\) it is empty over \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).  Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}stengle\text{-}semialgebraic\text{-}emptiness}\) over that real closed field.  It supplies finite polynomials \(a_0,b_0,c_0\) satisfying
\[
 a_0\in\langle E\rangle,
 \qquad b_0\in\operatorname{PO}(G),
 \qquad c_0\in\operatorname{Mon}(H),
 \qquad a_0+b_0+c_0^2=0.
\]
Only finitely many algebraic coefficients occur, so they lie in one finite real algebraic extension of \(\mathbb Q\).  Enumerating finite algebraic coefficient descriptions, ideal multipliers, sums-of-squares preordering representations, and monoid words eventually finds this identity.  Expanding both sides and reducing all coefficients in the finite extension verifies it exactly.  Conversely, evaluation at a point of \(S(E,G,H)\) would give \(a_0=0\), \(b_0\geq0\), and \(c_0^2>0\), contradicting the displayed identity.  Thus the identity is a sound, finite infeasibility certificate, completing both branches.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Theorem 1 (effect-specific positive-chamber separation decision).  For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), every \(D\in\mathfrak D\), and every outcome cell \(y\), define, for each bit-zero conditional-independence statement \(c\),
\[
 h_c(p)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal C_0(\mathcal I,c)}g(p)^2.
\]
There is a terminating exact real-closed-field decision procedure for the sentence
\[
 \exists p\in\mathbb R^\Omega\left[
 \sum_{z\in\Omega}p_z=1
 \ \wedge\ 
 \bigwedge_{g\in\mathcal C_1(\mathcal I)}g(p)=0
 \ \wedge\ 
 \bigwedge_{z\in\Omega}p_z>0
 \ \wedge\ 
 \bigwedge_{c:\mathcal I(c)=0}h_c(p)>0
 \ \wedge\ 
 F_{D,y}(p)\neq0
 \right].
\]
Exactly one of the following certificates is returned.  If the sentence is feasible, the procedure returns an exact real-algebraic table \(p^\dagger\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}^\Omega\), with minimal-polynomial and isolating data, such that
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^\dagger)\neq T_{D_0,y}(p^\dagger).
\]
If the sentence is infeasible, it returns a finite quantifier-elimination trace or Positivstellensatz identity proving
\[
 T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p)
 \qquad\text{for every }p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}.
\]
Thus feasibility, rather than nonmembership of \(F_{D,y}\) in the saturated real-radical ideal, is the complete positive exact-oracle separation criterion.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original implication from saturated-real-radical nonmembership to a bounded-height rational point is false without a hypothesis selecting the positive exact-oracle chamber. The replacement decides that chamber directly and weakens the general witness type only to an exactly checkable real-algebraic table.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Theorem 2 (SparseSIM-ID semialgebraic completeness).  For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) terminates after finite exact preprocessing and at most
\[
 |\mathfrak D|\prod_{v\in Y}|\Omega_v|
\]
real-closed-field feasibility decisions.  It returns exactly one of two mutually exclusive certificates: either the observable arithmetic circuit \(\tau=(T_{D_0,y})_y\), together with a finite real-radical or semialgebraic infeasibility certificate proving
\[
 T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p)
 \quad\text{for every }D\in\mathfrak D,\ y,\text{ and }p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ},
\]
or a triple \((D_0,D,p^\dagger)\) with an exact real-algebraic, strictly positive table
\[
 p^\dagger\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}^\Omega
\]
such that \((T_{D,y}(p^\dagger))_y\neq(T_{D_0,y}(p^\dagger))_y\).  The first branch occurs if and only if the intervention law is common to every represented DAG on the exact-oracle model.  Conditions \(\operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})=0\) provide a sufficient fast equality branch; every nonzero normal form is resolved by the positive-chamber feasibility decision and is not by itself interpreted as ambiguity.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The old termination proof depended on the unjustified bounded rational-point implication. The replacement removes that implication and its height and candidate-count guarantees, while giving unconditional termination through finitely many exact semialgebraic decisions.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Accept only a tuple certified by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), and construct the finite family of rational circuits \(T_{D,y}\) and polynomial signatures \(F_{D,y}\).  Compute the zero or nonzero status of each fixed-order normal form \(\operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})\) by exact real-radical membership or its equivalent real-closed-field decision.  If every normal form is zero, output the reference circuit \((T_{D_0,y})_y\) together with finite real-Nullstellensatz and saturation identities.  Otherwise first test the supplied rational exact-oracle witness \(p^{\circ}\); if some \(F_{D,y}(p^{\circ})\neq0\), return \((D_0,D,p^{\circ})\).  For every remaining pair \((D,y)\) with nonzero normal form, in canonical order decide the basic semialgebraic formula \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) and \(F_{D,y}(p)\neq0\) by a fixed exact real-closed-field quantifier-elimination or cylindrical algebraic decomposition procedure.  At the first feasible formula, return \((D_0,D,p^\dagger)\), where \(p^\dagger\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}^\Omega\) is encoded by a rational univariate representation, coordinate minimal polynomials, and isolating or Thom data.  If every such formula is infeasible, output the reference circuit, using real-radical identities for the zero-normal-form pairs and finite quantifier-elimination traces or Positivstellensatz identities for the remaining pairs.  A nonzero normal form is only a trigger for the positive-chamber feasibility test and is never itself reported as an ambiguity certificate.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: A nonzero saturated-real-radical normal form need not meet the strictly positive exact-oracle sign chamber. The algorithm must replace bounded rational enumeration by exact positive-chamber feasibility, retaining zero normal forms only as a sufficient fast branch.

proposed.gap: Saturation results do not select the positive exact-oracle chamber, and existing simultaneous-identification criteria do not supply a rational-density bridge; exact semialgebraic feasibility closes the decision problem without either claim.

prose_updates.tldr: Observational discovery can return several non-Markov-equivalent graphs with the same minimum edge count, and selecting one can change \(P_x(Y)\). SparseSIM-ID checks a nonempty certified tied family and a positive rational realization of the exact CI oracle, compiles every represented DAG's truncated factorization into a rational observed-table circuit, and then decides effect agreement on the strictly positive exact-oracle chamber. Fixed-order real-radical zero tests are a fast sufficient branch; otherwise exact real-closed-field feasibility returns either the common circuit with finite infeasibility certificates or an exact real-algebraic ambiguity table with isolating data. The certified four-binary-variable instance remains a rational strictness witness beyond the sufficient test of Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo, and pointwise multinomial delta-method inference applies to a fixed certified equality-branch circuit.

project_justification.gap: Existing simultaneous-identification theory gives sufficient graphical conditions but not a necessary decision of common effects on the strictly positive exact-oracle law model. Saturated CI ideals alone do not select that sign chamber.
project_justification.niche: Minimum-edge ties are a structured and operationally important family in which graph-local Markov constraints are redundant. Common-effect identification therefore reduces to finitely many graph-indexed rational-function equalities tested on one explicit semialgebraic exact-oracle chamber.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a complete exact semialgebraic decision algorithm: each intervention signature is either infeasible off zero on the positive exact-oracle chamber, with a finite quantifier-elimination or Positivstellensatz certificate, or has an exact real-algebraic positive separator. It retains real-radical normal forms as a fast sufficient test, proves strictness over the closest graphical criterion with a concrete rational four-node witness, and attaches fixed-input plug-in inference to the common circuit.

prose_updates.related_work: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo (Proceedings of the 42nd ICML, 2025, Theorem 3.2 and Section 4.2) give the closest causal boundary: their SA-MPDAG criterion is sufficient, and their necessity discussion requires a common law with unequal graphwise effects, but supplies no general rational-density or positive-chamber construction. Theorem 2 decides every certified tied-sparsest query, while Corollary 1 retains a positive rational instance on which their graphical test is undecided. Perkovic (2020, Theorem 3.6) supplies the graph-specific bucket truncated factorization adapted here into rational observed-cell circuits. Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels (2005, Theorem 8) inform saturation by marginal factors, but saturation does not select the strictly positive exact-oracle chamber or impose the bit-zero inequalities. Tarski's real-closed-field decision method and Stengle's Positivstellensatz supply the generic exact feasibility and infeasibility machinery used after the graph-native compilation. Kahle, Rauh, and Sullivant (2017, Sections 3.1 and 3.3) explain why irrelevant CI components make positivity separate from ideal membership. Raskutti and Uhler (2018) define the tied minimum-edge discovery target without an effect-aware output policy. Guo and Perkovic (2021, Theorem 3), Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2019, Section 4.2), and Duarte et al. (2024) respectively inform within-MPDAG effect quotienting, success-or-obstruction completeness, and certified polynomial compilation. Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2024) motivate the distinction between discovery and estimation uncertainty; the plug-in theorem remains pointwise for one fixed certified population input.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The complete decision is finite but carries no useful uniform complexity or algebraic-height bound. Saturation by cells and denominators excludes components contained in their zero sets, but it neither imposes \(p_z>0\) nor the nonvanishing blocks for zero CI bits; consequently \(F_{D,y}\notin K_{\mathcal I}\) is only a trigger for semialgebraic testing and never an ambiguity certificate. A feasible general witness is guaranteed to be exactly real algebraic, not rational. Rational output with a uniform height bound remains the separate rational-atlas open question.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact CI oracle, background orientations, query, complete tied minimum-edge family, and a positive rational exact-oracle feasibility witness are fixed certified population inputs; empty graph families and unrealizable exact oracles are outside the accepted domain. The main result is complete semialgebraic decidability with exact real-algebraic separator output, not a general rational-point theorem and not a polynomial-time guarantee. The existing rational-atlas open question records whether every separating chamber admits a bounded-height rational witness. The four-variable certified table remains an explicit rational separator with minimum cell \(1/40\), exactly four elementary CIs, \(50\) I-map DAGs, exactly two four-edge minima in distinct MECs, and intervention probabilities \(13/20\) and \(1/2\). When the candidate family is one MPDAG and the oracle model equals that graph's positive Markov model, the decision specializes to the known single-family setting. Plug-in inference fixes one certified equality-branch circuit and one interior law; it is not selection-aware inference for an estimated oracle or graph tie set.

statement_notes.justification: This is the load-bearing positive-chamber decision: it distinguishes universal equality from a graph-indexed causal separator using exact, independently checkable semialgebraic certificates.
statement_notes.gap: Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels do not select the strictly positive exact-oracle chamber, and Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo provide no general density construction producing a rational separator there.
statement_notes.consumer: A discovery package can return either a verified common effect or an exact real-algebraic ambiguity table encoded by minimal polynomials and isolating data.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem replaces arbitrary selection among tied sparsest graphs by an unconditional common-functional-or-exact-counterexample decision contract.
statement_notes.gap: Sufficient graphical tests leave some tied-family queries unresolved, while a nonzero saturated-real-radical remainder does not decide the relevant positive sign chamber.
statement_notes.consumer: Tetrad SP and causaldag or GSP all-ties output can report a common effect circuit with infeasibility certificates or an exact real-algebraic ambiguity table instead of choosing one tied graph.
